To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the moving average rule's performance is due to both linear and non-linear relationships between past and future stock returns.
the MA trading rule exploits linear dependencies in stock prices.
a substantial part (up to 80%) of the predictive performance of MA trading rules is due to the existence of linear dependencies in the stock returns.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the predictive performance of a trading rule of technical trading, the moving average ( MA) rule, in the context of the Efficient Market Hypothesis.

the decomposition of the predictive performance of MA trading rules and with the attribution of the rule's success to the exploitation of the linear and the non-linear dependencies in the time series of stock returns.
decomposing the predictive power of the moving average rule of technical analysis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
MA rules are not able to generate excess returns from non-linear dependencies in financial data.
the MA trading rule is able to exploit both the linear and the non-linear dependencies of stock returns.

the predictive performance that can be attributed to linear dependencies is more pronounced for short MA lengths, whereas for long MA lengths it is more likely that the predictive performance is due mainly to the exploitation of non-linear dependencies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the predictive performance is mainly due to the exploitation (by the MA rule) of linear dependencies in returns and that the non-linear dependencies in returns do not contribute to the predictive performance of this particular trading rule.
the MA rule is not only exploiting the linear dependencies in stock prices but also the non-linear ones.
the moving average rule of technical analysis is not only based on linear dependencies in stock prices but also on non-linear dependencies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the MA trading rule is a linear trading rule.
the predictive performance that is usually attributed to the MA trading rule of technical trading is due to the combination of linear and non-linearity in stock returns and not to the rule itself.
the predictive performance that has been attributed to the MA rule in the literature is not solely due to the rule's ability to predict the direction of future stock returns.
